name: online-offline-pack-architecture
description: Split AI capabilities into online and offline packs with clear handoff protocols for connectivity continuity
steps: Identify which capabilities require internet (APIs, cloud services, real-time data)
Identify which capabilities work locally (file search, local LLM, mesh networking)
Assign hounds to online pack (cloud-connected) or offline pack (local-first)
Create hybrid hounds for tasks that bridge both (scheduling, task queuing)
Design handoff protocols for transitions (online→offline, offline→online)
Establish surrogate roles (e.g., offline hound replaces online hound when disconnected)
Document connectivity requirements for each capability
examples: Online: Newton (arXiv), Tracker (OSINT databases), Budger (Alpaca API)
Offline: Toby (local files), Builder (mesh), Pupper (local LLM)
Hybrid: Corraler (queues online tasks, runs offline tasks always)
Surrogate: Pupper replaces Shepherd when offline
Handoff: Newton research flows to Toby for offline access
